meaning: Reviewed operation obligations and selected assertions, not a completion certificate or replacement-provider certification.

operations.obligation: Binding identifies one selected store incarnation and open session; declared limits validate. Invalid dependency tokens cannot change that binding or certify another store/session.
remaining: Concurrent multi-instance resource-pressure coverage beyond these two-store histories.

operations.obligation: Return verified durable state for the exact group incarnation; missing is an error. Admission alone does not advance the durable view. Recovery preserves the acknowledged state.
remaining: Broader checkpoint/membership combinations and generated corruption/recovery histories beyond the selected old-checkpoint cases.

operations.obligation: Consume the caller-owned mutation batch and return exact per-group admission tickets, not durability evidence. Each group transition preserves committed history and binds dependent hard state; deterministic rejection leaves the durable state unchanged. Accepted writes are not undone by dropping a wait.
remaining: General independently failing per-group batches for future backends; these providers implement stronger atomic batch recovery.

operations.obligation: Certify only the supplied exact accepted tickets in the same domain: store identity/incarnation/session, group identity/incarnation, batch, revision, generation, last index and term. Invalid tokens retain genuine pending work. Uncertain persistence fences the store until explicit recovery; there is no cancel/rollback operation.
remaining: Broader generated device/sync failure schedules and future backend conformance. Physical sync may cover more bytes than the explicit returned evidence.

operations.obligation: Return ordered durable entries within the selected generation and count/byte budget. Reject stale suffix generations and invalid boundaries. Refuse an oversized first entry instead of violating the budget; snapshot compaction reports its floor.
remaining: Generated boundary/capacity histories and future backend coverage.

operations.obligation: Declare optional physical reclamation. Unsupported calls fail without mutation. Reject outstanding transitions and insufficient budgets. Successful cleanup preserves every group's current durable state and snapshot references, does not move the logical retention floor and issues no new durability ticket.
remaining: General retention/segment policy and wider disk-full/device failure combinations.

operations.obligation: Identify the exact store/group incarnations and open session, with validated application/chunk bounds. Recovery keeps durable identity and changes the admission session.
remaining: Broader limit combinations and concurrent shared-resource pressure.

operations.obligation: Admit one bounded stage for the selected group. Reject zero/oversized payloads, changed group, non-increasing history or occupied retained slots without altering the published image.
remaining: Generated metadata/membership and capacity combinations; native metadata encoding budgets have separate tests.

operations.obligation: Accept only the exact active ticket and ordered nonempty bounded chunks. Reject all changed identity/session/generation fields and wrong offset/size without consuming genuine work.
remaining: Generated chunk partitions and device failures beyond the existing native interruption suite.

operations.obligation: Only a complete exact stage can be synchronized and sealed. Sealing does not publish or supersede the old root. Reject stale and repeated seals.
remaining: Shared host conformance does not certify physical synchronization; future providers need their own device fault adapter.

operations.obligation: Publish only the exact synchronized ticket, file length and checksum. Reject altered or foreign receipts without consuming the original stage. Preserve original metadata/data together; uncertainty fences native use until recovery.
remaining: Broader membership/lifecycle compositions and alternative provider publication failures.

operations.obligation: Discard only the exact active stage, before or after seal, without changing the published root. A stale session cannot cancel a fresh stage. Abort after publication is not rollback.
remaining: Asynchronous worker cancellation is a distinct contract, not established by these synchronous cases.

operations.obligation: Return the verified published metadata/application pair or explicitly empty new store. Unpublished stages remain invisible after file close/reopen. Missing/corrupt durable state is an error.
remaining: File close/reopen is not hardware power-loss validation; native modeled failures and wider device tests remain distinct.

operations.obligation: Return the exact current published durable reference, independent of transient admission session. Reconciliation selects the authoritative pinned root or clears it.
remaining: Broader interrupted manifest updates and future backend recovery coverage.

operations.obligation: Pin a verified exact published image before the caller records a durable log boundary. Repeated pins are idempotent; altered identity, generation, metadata, length or checksum cannot create an anchor. Anchored slots cannot be overwritten.
remaining: Cases supply the authoritative-log caller role; they do not themselves commit a WAL boundary.

operations.obligation: Retrieve the exact retained image even after another root is published and after file reopen. Reject every modified reference field and released anchor.
remaining: Further corruption of old retained slots and combined membership changes need wider device/fault coverage.

operations.obligation: Select only the caller-supplied exact pinned durable-log reference and release other anchors. Reject unknown references or a pending stage without mutating pins/root. None releases all anchors and clears the root.
remaining: Caller must establish its authoritative durable log reference; general retention policy and combined interrupted WAL/manifest histories remain.

operations.obligation: Fixed authoritative WAL store/session and worker generation scope every accepted ticket. Visit identity and original request must match before an owner consumes a completion.
remaining: Future external worker implementations need the same cases; callers must choose a fresh generation.

operations.obligation: Validate configured bounds and report stable selected-group image/application allowances. Unassigned groups report no allowance and are refused before I/O.
remaining: Broader combinations of allocation capacity, load bounds and provider scratch memory.

operations.obligation: Retain request/image credits until terminal polling, including after close and while a result awaits observation. Release only the completed request; return zero usage when drained.
remaining: General fairness and pressure across additional shared executors.

operations.obligation: Return the exact original work and image allocation on rejection. Admit one request per group with nonzero increasing scoped sequence; reject foreign bindings, unassigned groups and post-close work without changing usage.
remaining: Cancellation is not rollback: this contract has no per-request cancellation method.

operations.obligation: Return bounded exact request/visit completions. Publication pins and verifies actual data before success; readiness/load/reconcile preserve exact references. Obsolete envelopes cannot release a live owner lease or fence its current core.
remaining: Existing native failures are selected histories; future providers need independent crash/failure adapters and wider combined schedules.

operations.obligation: Stop new admissions, retain and drain accepted work, and do not roll back acknowledged publication when the owner observation is discarded. Native reclaim joins its own worker and returns the selected stores only after terminal polling.
remaining: The new shared worker cases use the native executor with host/file stores; the core-only downstream worker exercises separate envelope/failure cases. Shared external executor lifetime remains provider-specific.
